answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with reputation staking: every identity locks real value, and its transaction history sits on a public ledger that peers inspect like a mirror, so identical behavior across supposedly independent accounts betrays one operator. New identities earn capacity only through costly, verifiable work, so mass forgery never pays. Like timber, trust grows slowly but burns fast: a detected sybil loses its stake and leaves a crystal trace honest agents share as a blacklist.
